memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: To the woman he said, "I will make your pains in childbearing very severe; with painful labor you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you." — Gen 3:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard verse, and we should not rush past its weight. Sin's entry into the world does not leave a single part of life untouched — not even the most beautiful ones. Childbirth, the bringing of new life into the world, now comes wrapped in pain. And marriage, meant to be a partnership of joy and unity (Gen 2:24), now carries tension and struggle between husband and wife.

We must be careful how we read this. God is not laying down a command for how things ought to be, but describing the painful reality of a world now broken by sin. The closeness that should mark marriage will be strained; harmony will not come easily. This is a description of the fall's damage, not God's design for how men and women should treat one another.

And yet even here, grace whispers. God says the woman will still bring forth children — life goes on. The human family does not end. And it is through this very line, through the offspring of the woman, that the promised Saviour will one day come (Gen 3:15; Gal 4:4).

Dear friend, we live in a world where even our sweetest gifts are touched by pain — relationships strain, joys carry sorrow. But this is not how the story ends. In Christ, what sin fractured is being made whole again, and one day every pain will be wiped away completely (Rev 21:4). The brokenness is real, but it is not forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you felt the ache of pain mixed into something meant to be good?
2. How does it help to see this verse as describing a broken world rather than God's design for it?
3. How does the hope of Christ's restoration steady you in the strains of daily life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I feel the weight of living in a world where even good gifts are touched by pain. Thank You that You have not abandoned us to the brokenness, but sent Jesus to make all things new. Give me hope in the strains of life, knowing You are restoring what sin has broken. Amen.
